items.title: Four Names for the Intermediate Being

items.zh: 又此中有，有種種名。或名中有，在死生二有中間生故。或名健達縛，尋香行故，香所資故。或名意行，以意為依，往生處故。此說身往，非心緣往。或名趣生，對生有起故。
items.en: Further, this intermediate being has various names. It is called "the between-existence," because it arises between the existence of death and the existence of birth. It is called a gandharva, because it travels in search of scent, and is nourished by scent. It is called "mind-gone," because, taking mind as its support, it travels to the place of its birth — this refers to an actual going of the [subtle] body, not merely a mental reaching-towards. It is called "heading towards birth," because it arises in anticipation of the existence to come.

items.zh: 當知中有除無色界一切生處。又造惡業者，謂屠羊雞猪等，隨其一類，由住不律儀眾同分故，作感那落迦惡不善業及增長已。
items.en: It should be understood that the intermediate existence occurs in every place of birth except the formless realm. Further, 'one who does evil deeds' means a butcher of sheep, chickens, pigs, and the like: belonging to one such group and living among those bound to non-restraint, they have done and accumulated evil, unwholesome karma that leads to the hells.

items.title: Drawn In by Illusion: How Rebirth Actually Happens

items.zh: 彼於爾時，猶如夢中，自於彼業所得生處，還見如是種類有情及屠羊等事。由先所習，喜樂馳趣，即於生處境色所礙，中有遂滅，生有續起。彼將沒時，如先死有，見紛亂色。如是乃至生滅道理，如前應知。又彼生時，唯是化生，六處具足。復起是心，而往趣之。謂我與彼嬉戲受樂，習諸伎藝。彼於爾時顛倒，謂造種種事業，及觸冷熱。
items.en: At that time, as though in a dream, one sees, in the very place one's karma has determined for one's birth, beings of that same kind, engaged in that same [unwholesome] activity. Because of what was long practised before, one is drawn there with delight, and, obstructed by the sights of that place, the intermediate being then ceases, and the existence of birth arises in its place. This thought then arises: "I am playing there with them, enjoying myself, practising our old skills together." At that time one is deluded, believing oneself to be actually performing these various activities, and actually feeling cold and heat.

items.zh: 若離妄見，如是相貌尚無趣欲，何況往彼。若不往彼，便不應生。如於那落迦如是，於餘似那落迦鬼趣中生，當知亦爾，
items.en: Were this false view abandoned, not even the desire to approach such an appearance would arise — how much less the actual going there. And if one does not go there, one would not be born there at all. As with hell, so it should be understood with rebirth among ghosts of a hell-like kind.

items.zh: 如癭鬼等。
items.en: Such as goitre ghosts and the like.

items.zh: 又於餘鬼、傍生、人等，及欲、色界天眾同分中將受生時，於當生處，見己同類可意有情，由此於彼起其欣欲，即往生處，便被拘礙。
items.en: Further, when about to be born among the remaining realms — ghosts, animals, humans, or the desire- and form-realm heavens — at the very place of one's birth, one sees beings of one's own kind who appear agreeable, and from this a longing to join them arises. One then goes to that place of birth, and is thereby caught and held fast there.

items.zh: 死生道理，如前應知。
items.en: The principle of death and rebirth should be understood as before.

items.title: Entering the Womb: Three Conditions, Three Obstructions

items.zh: 又由三處現前，得入母胎。一、其母調適，而復值時；二、父母和合，俱起愛染；三、健達縛正現在前。復無三種障礙。謂產處過患所作，種子過患所作，宿業過患所作。
items.en: Further, only when three conditions are present at once can one enter the mother's womb: first, the mother is healthy, and it is the fertile time; second, the father and mother come together, both moved by desire; third, the gandharva is actually present. There must, moreover, be none of three obstructions: those caused by a defect of the birth-canal, those caused by a defect of the seed, and those caused by a defect of past karma.

items.zh: 云何產處過患？謂若產處為風熱癊之所逼迫；或於其中有麻麥果；或復其門如車螺形，有形有曲，有穢有濁。如是等類，產處過患應知。
items.en: What is a defect of the birth-canal? It is when the birth-canal is afflicted by wind, heat, or phlegm; or when something like a hemp-seed or a barley-grain grows within it; or when its opening is shaped like a cart or a conch shell, malformed, twisted, foul, or turbid. Defects of this and similar kinds should be understood as defects of the birth-canal.

items.zh: 云何種子過患？謂父出不淨非母，或母非父，或俱不出；或父精朽爛，或母，或俱。如是等類，種子過患應知。
items.en: What is a defect of the seed? It is when the father emits seed but not the mother, or the mother but not the father, or neither does so; or when the father's seed has decayed, or the mother's, or both. Defects of this and similar kinds should be understood as defects of the seed.

items.zh: 云何宿業過患？謂或父或母不作、不增長感子之業，或復俱無。或彼有情不作、不增長感父母業。或彼父母作及增長感餘子業。
items.en: What is a defect of past karma? It is when either the father or the mother, or both, have not created and built up the karma that would draw a child to them; or when that being has not created and built up the karma that would draw these particular parents; or when the parents have created and built up karma that draws a different being as their child.

items.zh: 或彼有情作及增長感餘父母業。或感大宗葉業。或感非大宗葉業。如是等類，宿業過患應知。若無如是三種過患，三處現前，得入母胎。
items.en: Or that being has done and accumulated karma that leads to other parents; or karma that leads to birth in a great family; or karma that leads to birth in a family that is not great. Faults such as these should be understood as faults of past karma. If none of these three kinds of fault is present and the three conditions are present, the being is able to enter the mother's womb.

items.zh: 彼即於中有處，自見與己同類有情為嬉戲等。於所生處起希趣欲。彼於爾時，見其父母共行邪行所出精血而起顛倒。起顛倒者，謂見父母為邪行時，不謂父母行此邪行，乃起倒覺、見己自行。見自行已，便起貪愛。
items.en: While still an intermediate being, one sees, as it were, beings of one's own kind at play, and a longing to go to that place of birth arises. At that time, seeing one's father and mother engaged in intercourse and the fluids they produce, a delusion arises: instead of perceiving that it is one's parents engaged in this act, a distorted perception arises in which one sees oneself performing it. Having seen oneself performing it, craving then arises.

items.zh: 若當欲為女，彼即於父便起會貪；若當欲為男，彼即於母起貪亦爾。乃往逼趣。若女於母，欲其遠去；若男於父，心亦復爾。生此欲已，或唯見男，或唯見女。如如漸近彼之處所，如是如是漸漸不見父母餘分，唯見男女根門。即於此處便被拘礙。
items.en: If one is about to become female, craving for union with the father arises; if one is about to become male, craving for union with the mother arises in just the same way. One then draws close, driven by this craving. If female, one wishes the mother would go away; if male, the same holds for the father. Once this craving has arisen, one sees only the father, or only the mother; and the closer one draws to that place, the more the rest of the parent's form fades from sight, until only the male or female organ remains visible. It is there that one becomes caught and held fast.

items.zh: 死生道理，如是應知。
items.en: The principle of death and rebirth should be understood in this way.

items.zh: 若薄福者，當生下賤家。彼於死時及入胎時，便聞種種紛亂之聲，及自妄見入於叢林、竹𥯤、蘆𥭳等中。若多福者，當生尊貴家。彼於爾時，便自聞有寂靜美妙可意音聲，及自妄見昇宮殿等可意相現。
items.en: One of little merit, about to be born into a humble family, hears at death and at the moment of entering the womb a confused clamour of sounds, and falsely perceives oneself entering a thicket, a stand of reeds, or tall grass. One of great merit, about to be born into a noble family, hears at that same time a tranquil and beautiful sound, and falsely perceives oneself ascending into a palace or some other agreeable scene.

items.title: Conception: The Kalala Stage and the Body's First Foothold

items.zh: 爾時父母貪愛俱極，最後決定各出一滴濃厚精血。二滴和合住母胎中，合為一段。猶如熟乳凝結之時。當於此處，一切種子異熟所攝執受所依阿賴耶識和合依託。云何和合依託？謂此所出濃厚精血合成一段，與顛倒緣中有俱滅。與滅同時，即由一切種子識功能力故，有餘微細根及大種和合而生，及餘有根同分精血和合摶生。於此時中，說識已住結生相續。即此名為羯羅藍位。
items.en: At that time, when the father's and mother's craving both reach their height, each finally emits a single drop of concentrated fluid. The two drops unite within the mother's womb and form a single mass, like curdled milk at the moment it sets. It is here that the ālayavijñāna — the ripened-effect consciousness that holds all seeds and appropriates its support — comes to unite with and rest upon this mass. This concentrated fluid, having formed into a single mass, ceases together with the deluded, craving intermediate being. At the very moment of this cessation, through the functional power of the all-seeds consciousness, the subtle faculties and the great elements arise together in union, and the body-faculty, together with fluid of the same kind, arises massed together with them. At this time, consciousness is said to have taken up residence, binding this existence into continuity. This is called the kalala stage.

items.zh: 此羯羅藍中，有諸根大種、唯與身根及根所依處大種俱生。
items.en: In this kalala, the great elements of the sense faculties arise only together with the body faculty and with the great elements of the places that support the faculties.

items.zh: 即由此身根俱生諸根大種力故，眼等諸根次第當生。又由此身根俱生根所依處大種力故，諸根依處次第當生。由彼諸根及所依處具足生故，名得圓滿依止成就。
items.en: Through the power of the faculty-elements arising together with this body-faculty, the eye and the other faculties come to arise in sequence. And through the power of the elements underlying their supports, arising together with this same body-faculty, the physical supports of these faculties likewise come to arise in sequence. Once these faculties and their supports have fully arisen, this is called the attainment of complete bodily support.

items.zh: 又此羯羅藍色，與心心所安危共同，故名依託。由心心所依託力故，色不爛壞；色損益故，彼亦損益；是故說彼安危共同。又此羯羅藍識最初託處，即名肉心。如是識於此處最初託，即從此處最後捨。
items.en: This kalala matter, moreover, shares one fate with the mind and its mental factors, safe when they are safe and endangered when they are endangered — hence it is called their "support." Through the supporting power of mind and its mental factors, the matter does not decay; and as the matter is diminished or enhanced, so too are they — hence they are said to share one fate. Further, the place where consciousness first takes hold of this kalala is called the flesh-heart. Just as consciousness first takes hold here, so it is from this very place that consciousness departs last of all.

blocks.text: This is the last reading of fascicle 1. It finishes the account of rebirth: the intermediate being's names, how it is drawn to its place of birth, the conditions for entering the womb, and the first moment of the new life, the **kalala** (羯羅藍). Master Cháng Bǎi stresses that the passage is not embryology for its own sake. It shows, step by step, that a new existence is driven by craving and false perception, not by choice or by an outside power.

Several short passages are missing from Ru-Yi's translation, and we have supplied our own: 0282b08–b11 (the intermediate existence in every realm but the formless; a butcher's karma leading to hell); 0282b21 ("such as goitre ghosts"); 0282b25 and 0282c25 ("the principle of death and rebirth should be understood as before"); 0282c11–c14 (more karmic obstructions, and entry into the womb when none is present); and 0283a10–a11 (the elements present in the kalala).

The intermediate being is called "the between-existence" (中有), because it lies between death and birth; a **gandharva** (健達縛), "scent-eater", because it is nourished by scent; "mind-gone" (意行), because it travels by mental power; and "seeking existence" (求生), because it is always looking for its next birth. Each name picks out one feature of the same thing.

"As though in a dream", the being sees in the place its karma has determined beings of its own kind doing what it once did, and is drawn there with delight. Then comes the key sentence: "Were this false view abandoned, not even the desire to approach such an appearance would arise, how much less the actual going there. And if one does not go there, one would not be born there at all."

No judge sends the being anywhere; it goes because of what it mistakenly finds attractive. Venerable Miào Jìng draws a lesson for meditators: both agreeable and disagreeable scenes are false views, to be seen through by calm, insight, and wisdom. Training now in not being carried away by appearances is training for that moment.

Conception requires three conditions at once: a healthy mother at the fertile time, both parents moved by desire, and the gandharva present. It also requires the absence of three defects: of the birth-canal, of the "seed", and of past karma.

Watch the word "seed" here. Venerable Miào Jìng, citing the *Pīxún jì*: "This is not a seed; it is only provisionally called a seed. The real seed is this being's own linguistic perfuming." The parents' fluids are only a contributing condition. Master Cháng Bǎi calls it a borrowed term, as a grain is loosely called the "seed" of a sprout. This is another terminology trap: in most of the treatise, **seed** (種子) means the potential held in the ālayavijñāna.

The defect of karma is equally telling. The parents must have the karma to have *this* child, and the child the karma to have *these* parents. Birth is a meeting of karmic connections, not an accident.

Seeing its future parents, the being does not perceive them as they are; it perceives only its own desire, attraction to one parent and wish that the other were gone, until the whole field of vision narrows to a single point and it is "caught and held fast". Both the being of little merit, which hears clamour and seems to enter a thicket, and the being of great merit, which hears beautiful sounds and seems to enter a palace, are perceiving falsely. Venerable Miào Jìng: "they don't know that they are entering a womb."

The parents' fluids unite "like curdled milk at the moment it sets". At that moment the ālayavijñāna, "the ripened-effect consciousness that holds all seeds and appropriates its support", takes hold of this mass. The intermediate being ceases at the same moment: again the two ends of the scale. Through the power of the all-seeds consciousness, the body-faculty arises first, and from it, in sequence, the other faculties and their physical bases. This first stage of the embryo is called the **kalala**, the first of eight stages in the womb that fascicle 2 will describe.

Here we meet again the word **appropriate** (執受) from Day 1. Matter and mind now share "one fate", safe together and endangered together: consciousness keeps the matter from decaying, and harm to the matter harms them in turn. That shared fate is what it means for the ālayavijñāna to appropriate a body.

The place where consciousness first takes hold is called the **flesh-heart** (肉心), and "just as consciousness first takes hold here, so it is from this very place that consciousness departs last of all". This closes a circle opened on Day 5: life begins and ends at the same point. Venerable Miào Jìng adds a personal opinion: older translations took the flesh-heart as the physical heart, but, following the Theravāda view that the mind-faculty is based in the brain, he thinks "brain" also makes sense, since the brain in turn depends on the heart. Ru-Yi keeps the literal "flesh-heart".

In six days we have moved from a single moment of seeing to the whole arc of death and rebirth. The same few ideas carry everything: consciousness arises from seeds when conditions meet; the mental consciousness, through attention and volition, makes karma; and self-love and false perception carry the stream on. Fascicle 2 completes the Mind Stage's account of birth, then turns to the formation and destruction of the world.

quiz.q: The treatise says the intermediate being, as if in a dream, sees the scene at its place of birth and is drawn there with delight. What happens if this false view is abandoned?
options: it is still dragged into that birth by the force of karma
not even the desire to approach such an appearance would arise — how much less the actual going there; and if one does not go there, one would not be born there at all
one is certainly reborn in a heaven
one remains an intermediate being forever
quiz.why: "Were this false view abandoned, not even the desire to approach such an appearance would arise — how much less the actual going there. And if one does not go there, one would not be born there at all." This is the pivotal line of the passage: no outside force drags a being into its next life; it is drawn in by an illusory scene. Option A contradicts exactly this. Venerable Miào Jìng draws a practice lesson from it: those who meditate should recognise that agreeable and disagreeable situations alike are false views, to be seen through by calm, insight, and prajñā.

quiz.q: The treatise says one can enter the mother's womb only when three conditions are present at once. What are they?
options: the mother is healthy and it is the fertile time; the father and mother come together, both moved by desire; the gandharva is actually present
no defect of the birth-canal, no defect of the seed, no defect of past karma
attention properly arises, the faculty is unimpaired, the object is present
self-love, delight in elaboration, pure and impure karma
quiz.why: The three conditions are: the mother is healthy and it is the fertile time; the parents come together, both moved by desire; and the gandharva is actually present. Option B is the closest trap — it comes in the very next sentence, but as a separate list: the three *obstructions* that must be absent. C lists the conditions for eye-consciousness to arise in §14; D lists the causes of death and birth from §33–36.

quiz.q: One of the three obstructions to conception is "a defect of the seed." According to Venerable Miào Jìng (citing the Pixunji) and Master Cháng Bǎi, how should "seed" be understood here?
options: the linguistic seeds stored in the ālayavijñāna
the intermediate being's seed
"seed" is only a borrowed name here for the parents' reproductive fluids; the being's true seeds are its own linguistic perfuming
the seeds of grain or other plants
quiz.why: The defect of the seed is described as "when the father emits seed but not the mother, or the mother but not the father … or when the father's seed has decayed" — that is, the parents' reproductive fluids. Venerable Miào Jìng, citing the *Pixunji*, says: "This is not a seed; it is only provisionally called a 'seed.' The real seed is this being's own linguistic perfuming." The fluids are only a contributing condition. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise calls it a borrowed term, as a grain is loosely called the "seed" of a sprout. Option A is what "seed" properly means elsewhere in this fascicle — exactly the confusion to avoid here. The hemp-seed and barley-grain in D belong to the preceding item, the defect of the birth-canal.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does one of little merit, about to be born into a humble family, experience at death and at the moment of entering the womb?
options: hears a confused clamour of sounds, and falsely perceives oneself entering a thicket, a stand of reeds, or tall grass
hears a tranquil and beautiful sound, and falsely perceives oneself ascending into a palace
sees light like that off white cloth, like a clear, moonlit night
knows clearly that one is entering the womb
quiz.why: One of little merit "hears at death and at the moment of entering the womb a confused clamour of sounds, and falsely perceives oneself entering a thicket, a stand of reeds, or tall grass." Option B describes one of great merit, about to be born into a noble family. C is the light of a wholesome being's intermediate existence from §36, not a sign of conception. D is wrong: as Venerable Miào Jìng notes, both kinds of being are perceiving falsely — "they don't know that they are entering a womb."

quiz.q: When the two drops of the parents' fluid unite in the womb and form a single mass, what does the treatise compare it to?
options: like a lotus first opening
like a lamp flame first lit
like curdled milk at the moment it sets
like a drop of dew
quiz.why: "The two drops unite within the mother's womb and form a single mass, like curdled milk at the moment it sets." This is the kalala stage. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the term was rendered in older translations as "mixed impurity" or "congealed and slippery," and that it is the first of the eight stages in the womb. The other three options are not the treatise's images.

quiz.q: The treatise says, "The place where consciousness first takes hold of this kalala is called the flesh-heart." According to Venerable Miào Jìng, how should "flesh-heart" (肉心) be understood?
options: it can only mean the physical heart; there is no other view
older translations take it as the physical heart; he considers it reasonable, following the Theravāda view that the mind-faculty is the brain, to render it as "brain"
it is the ālayavijñāna itself
it is the body of the intermediate being
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The old translation took it as the heart, the organ. But modern people, following the Theravāda … hold that the mind-faculty on which mental consciousness depends is the brain. … I think rendering it as 'brain' makes sense." He adds that the brain in turn depends on the heart for its blood supply. Because this is his own leaning, the stem says "according to Venerable Miào Jìng"; the Ru-Yi translation keeps the literal "flesh-heart." Option C confuses the place where consciousness takes hold with consciousness itself — the flesh-heart is the matter the ālayavijñāna rests on, not the ālayavijñāna.
